405	    # -- account state Merkle tree -------------------------------------------
406	
407	    def _state_tree(
408	        self, chain: list | None = None
409	    ) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, int, list[str]]], list[str], str]:
410	        """Build the confirmed account rows (ascending account), their leaves
411	        and the Merkle root, all from the confirmed chain under the current
412	        endowment. ``chain`` defaults to the whole canonical chain; a confirmed
413	        prefix replays historical state deterministically. Caller must hold the
414	        store lock.
415	        """
416	        if chain is None:
417	            chain = self.store.chain
418	        rows = self.store.account_state_rows(chain, self.initial_balance)
419	        leaves = [
420	            crypto.account_state_leaf(account, balance, transactions)
421	            for account, balance, transactions in rows
422	        ]
423	        return rows, leaves, crypto.account_state_root(leaves)

425	    def get_state_root(self, height: object = None) -> tuple[int, dict]:
426	        """GET /v1/state/root and GET /v1/state/root/{height}.
427	
428	        Without a height the tree is anchored to the highest block. A pending
429	        chain tip anchors nothing yet, so the endpoint returns 404 until the
430	        tip is confirmed.
431	
432	        With a path height the state is replayed only from genesis through
433	        that block: the height must be an unsigned decimal without leading
434	        zeros (malformed heights are treated like any unknown path), the block
435	        must exist on the canonical chain and be confirmed — an unknown,
436	        non-canonical or pending height returns 404. The success body has
437	        exactly the same four fields as the unanchored endpoint.
438	        """
439	        with self.store.lock:
440	            if height is None:
441	                anchor = self.store.tip()
442	            else:
443	                # Strict unsigned decimal with no leading zeros, signs or
444	                # whitespace; every malformed value is an unknown path (404).
445	                height_int = _parse_decimal(height)
446	                if height_int is None:
447	                    return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
448	                anchor = self.store.block_at(height_int)
449	                if anchor is None:
450	                    return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
451	            if anchor.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
452	                return 404, {"error": "chain tip is pending confirmation"}
453	            prefix = self.store.chain if height is None else self.store.chain[: anchor.height + 1]
454	            rows, _leaves, root = self._state_tree(prefix)
455	            return 200, {
456	                "state_root": root,
457	                "height": anchor.height,
458	                "block_hash": anchor.block_hash,
459	                "account_count": len(rows),
460	            }

462	    def get_account_proof(
463	        self, account: str, params: dict | None = None
464	    ) -> tuple[int, dict]:
465	        """GET /v1/accounts/{account}/proof — an inclusion proof in the
466	        account-state tree.
467	
468	        Without ``height`` the proof is anchored to the highest (confirmed)
469	        block. With ``height=H`` the state is deterministically replayed from
470	        the canonical confirmed prefix through that block only: the value must
471	        be a plain non-negative decimal without leading zeros (a malformed or
472	        repeated query parameter is 400), and an unknown/non-canonical/pending
473	        anchor height is 404. Returns 404 while a pending tip anchors the
474	        default view, or for an account absent from the (historical) confirmed
475	        account set.
476	        """
477	        height_raw: object = None
478	        if params is not None:
479	            height_raw = params.get("height")
480	        anchor_height: int | None = None
481	        if height_raw is not None:
482	            anchor_height = _parse_decimal(height_raw)
483	            if anchor_height is None:
484	                return 400, {"error": "height must be a non-negative decimal"}
485	        with self.store.lock:
486	            if anchor_height is None:
487	                anchor = self.store.tip()
488	            else:
489	                anchor = self.store.block_at(anchor_height)
490	                if anchor is None:
491	                    return 404, {"error": "anchor block not found"}
492	            if anchor.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
493	                return 404, {"error": "chain tip is pending confirmation"}
494	            prefix = (
495	                self.store.chain
496	                if anchor_height is None
497	                else self.store.chain[: anchor.height + 1]
498	            )
499	            rows, leaves, root = self._state_tree(prefix)
500	            index = next(
501	                (i for i, (name, _b, _t) in enumerate(rows) if name == account),
502	                None,
503	            )
504	            if index is None:
505	                return 404, {"error": "account not found"}
506	            account_name, balance, transactions = rows[index]
507	            siblings = crypto.merkle_proof(leaves, index)
508	            return 200, {
509	                "account": account_name,
510	                "balance": balance,
511	                "confirmed_transactions": transactions,
512	                "index": index,
513	                "state_root": root,
514	                "height": anchor.height,
515	                "block_hash": anchor.block_hash,
516	                "siblings": siblings,
517	            }

519	    def confirmed_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
520	        """Balance from confirmed blocks only."""
521	        entry = self.store.accounts.get(account)
522	        if entry is None:
523	            return self.initial_balance
524	        return self.initial_balance + entry["received"] - entry["sent"]

526	    def reported_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
527	        """Confirmed balance minus spends sitting in the pending tip block.
528	
529	        Pending-block credits are not counted: unconfirmed income can still
530	        be rolled back, so it must not inflate the reported balance.
531	        """
532	        balance = self.confirmed_balance(account)
533	        tip = self.store.tip()
534	        if tip.status == STATUS_PENDING:
535	            for tx in tip.transactions:
536	                if tx.sender == account:
537	                    balance -= tx.amount
538	        return balance

540	    def available_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
541	        """Reported balance minus amounts already committed in the mempool.
542	
543	        Pending credits (mempool or unconfirmed block) are deliberately not
544	        counted, so a sequence of submissions cannot spend money that has not
545	        been confirmed yet.
546	        """
547	        balance = self.reported_balance(account)
548	        for tx in self.store.pending.values():
549	            if tx.sender == account:
550	                balance -= tx.amount
551	        return balance

553	    # -- fork candidates -----------------------------------------------------
554	
555	    @staticmethod
556	    def _fork_summary(blocks: list) -> dict:
557	        """Public fork descriptor S: tip_hash, height, length, status."""
558	        tip = blocks[-1]
559	        return {
560	            "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
561	            "height": tip.height,
562	            # The length counts every block including the genesis block.
563	            "length": len(blocks),
564	            "status": tip.status,
565	        }
566	
567	    def _winning_fork(self) -> tuple[str, list]:
568	        """Pick the winner among the canonical chain and every candidate.
569	
570	        Longest chain wins; equal lengths are broken by the smallest tip hash
571	        (lexicographic hex order). Returns (tip_hash, block list).
572	        """
573	        contenders: list[tuple[str, list]] = [
574	            (self.store.tip_hash(), self.store.chain)
575	        ]
576	        contenders.extend(self.store.forks.items())
577	        contenders.sort(key=lambda item: (-len(item[1]), item[0]))
578	        return contenders[0]
579	
580	    def submit_fork_candidate(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
581	        """POST /v1/forks/candidates — validate and store a candidate fork.
582	
583	        Returns 201 with the fork descriptor S. Malformed or invalid forks
584	        return 400; a fork already known (identical to the canonical tip or an
585	        existing candidate tip) returns 409.
586	        """
587	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
588	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
589	        blocks_raw = payload.get("blocks")
590	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
591	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: blocks (must be a list)"}
592	        try:
593	            fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
594	        except ValueError as exc:
595	            return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
596	        summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
597	        # An exported fork (the five-field {tip_hash, height, length, status,
598	        # blocks} document) may be resubmitted verbatim; every supplied summary
599	        # field is re-verified against the recomputed descriptor.
600	        for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
601	            if field in payload and payload[field] != summary[field]:
602	                return 400, {"error": f"summary field {field!r} does not match the blocks"}
603	        tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
604	        with self.store.lock:
605	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
606	            # A tip hash equal to any canonical block hash means the candidate
607	            # is exactly the canonical chain or a prefix of it (the block hash
608	            # binds height, parent and Merkle root), so it carries nothing new.
609	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
610	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
611	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:

642	    def adopt_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
643	        """POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — atomically switch to the winner.
644	
645	        Unknown tips return 404; adopting anything other than the current
646	        winning (longest / smallest-tip-hash) chain returns 409. Adoption
647	        replaces the canonical chain and mempool in one atomic write that
648	        advances the generation and rebuilds all indexes; transactions unique
649	        to the old chain's confirmed history return to the mempool, while
650	        pending-block transactions never enter it.
651	        """
652	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
653	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
654	        with self.store.lock:
655	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
656	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
657	            if fork is None:
658	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
659	            winner_tip, _ = self._winning_fork()
660	            if winner_tip != tip_hash:
661	                return 409, {"error": "only the winning fork can be adopted"}
662	            old_chain = self.store.chain
663	            old_pending = dict(self.store.pending)
664	            self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash)
665	            self.store.replace_chain(fork)
666	            # An adopted synced tip keeps its sync records (queryable until
667	            # expiry); record the adoption once per provenance entry. The
668	            # adopted tip summary is frozen from the adopted fork itself and
669	            # is never rewritten by later expiry.
670	            adopted_summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
671	            # The adopted tip may have provenance entries in the plain table,
672	            # the attested table, or both; each gets one adoption event.
673	            adopted: list[tuple[str | None, tuple[str, str]]] = []
674	            for skey in sorted(self.store.syncs):
675	                if self.store.syncs[skey]["tip_hash"] == tip_hash:
676	                    adopted.append((None, skey))
677	            for skey in sorted(self.store.attested_syncs):
678	                if self.store.attested_syncs[skey]["tip_hash"] == tip_hash:
679	                    adopted.append((SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED, skey))
680	            adopted_count = len(adopted)
681	            for rec_mode, (rec_source, request_id) in adopted:
682	                table = (
683	                    self.store.attested_syncs
684	                    if rec_mode is not None
685	                    else self.store.syncs
686	                )
687	                payload = {
688	                    "source": rec_source,
689	                    "request_id": request_id,
690	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
691	                    "expires_at": table[(rec_source, request_id)]["expires_at"],
692	                    "height": adopted_summary["height"],
693	                    "length": adopted_summary["length"],
694	                    "status": adopted_summary["status"],
695	                }
696	                if rec_mode is not None:
697	                    payload["mode"] = rec_mode
698	                self.store.append_audit_event(EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED, payload)
699	            try:
700	                self.store.save()
701	            except BaseException:
702	                # Restore the pre-adoption in-memory state on a failed write.
703	                self.store.chain = old_chain
704	                self.store.pending = old_pending
705	                self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
706	                self.store.rebuild_derived()
707	                self.store.truncate_audit_events(adopted_count)
708	                raise
709	            return 200, self._fork_summary(fork)

742	    def get_chain_range(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
743	        """GET /v1/chain/range — the canonical blocks strictly after an anchor.
744	
745	        Query parameters: ``after_height`` (a non-negative decimal anchor
746	        height) and ``after_hash`` (the anchor block's hash, 64 lowercase hex
747	        characters), both required, plus ``limit`` (default 100, range 1-500).
748	        Every value must follow the strict decimal/hex format used by the
749	        other query endpoints; a repeated parameter is rejected by the HTTP
750	        layer.
751	
752	        Returns, under the store lock,
753	        ``{anchor, blocks, canonical, next_height}``: ``anchor`` is
754	        ``{height, block_hash}`` naming the block the page starts *after*;
755	        ``blocks`` are the complete blocks following it (full documents
756	        including transactions; a pending tip block is exported too), up to
757	        ``limit``; ``canonical`` is the current chain descriptor S;
758	        ``next_height`` is the height immediately after the returned page, or
759	        ``null`` when the page already ends at the chain tip. A well-formed
760	        but unknown anchor height returns 404; a malformed anchor hash returns
761	        400; an anchor hash that does not match the block at that height
762	        returns 409.
763	        """
764	        after_height_raw = params.get("after_height")
765	        after_hash = params.get("after_hash")
766	        if after_height_raw is None:
767	            return 400, {"error": "missing parameter: after_height"}
768	        if after_hash is None:
769	            return 400, {"error": "missing parameter: after_hash"}
770	        after_height = _parse_decimal(after_height_raw)
771	        if after_height is None:
772	            return 400, {"error": "after_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
773	        if not crypto.is_hex64(after_hash):
774	            return 400, {"error": "after_hash must be 64 lowercase hex characters"}
775	        limit = self.RANGE_DEFAULT_LIMIT
776	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
777	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
778	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.RANGE_MAX_LIMIT:
779	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 500"}
780	            limit = parsed
781	
782	        with self.store.lock:
783	            anchor_block = self.store.block_at(after_height)
784	            if anchor_block is None:
785	                return 404, {"error": "anchor block not found"}
786	            if after_hash is not None and after_hash != anchor_block.block_hash:
787	                return 409, {
788	                    "error": "after_hash does not match the block at after_height"
789	                }
790	            page = self.store.chain[
791	                after_height + 1 : after_height + 1 + limit
792	            ]
793	            page_end_height = page[-1].height if page else anchor_block.height
794	            if page_end_height < self.store.chain[-1].height:
795	                next_height = page_end_height + 1
796	            else:
797	                next_height = None
798	            return 200, {
799	                "anchor": self._anchor_descriptor(anchor_block),
800	                "blocks": [block.to_dict() for block in page],
801	                "canonical": self._fork_summary(self.store.chain),
802	                "next_height": next_height,
803	            }

810	    @staticmethod
811	    def _candidate_blocks(candidate: object) -> object:
812	        """Normalize a sync ``candidate`` to its raw blocks list.
813	
814	        The candidate follows the existing export format (the five-field
815	        ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, blocks}`` document); the

818	        if isinstance(candidate, dict):

822	    @staticmethod
823	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
824	        """Stable content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
825	
826	        Used to decide whether a same-key retry carries the same candidate
827	        content. Key order and whitespace are normalized so two documents that
828	        serialize the same blocks identically compare equal.
829	        """
830	        return hashlib.sha256(
831	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

834	    def _prune_expired_syncs(self) -> list[str]:
835	        """Sweep expired sync records and persist the sweep atomically.
836	
837	        Both the plain and the attested record tables are swept together in a
838	        single atomic save that advances the generation. A candidate received
839	        through a sync lives only while a referencing record is unexpired; on
840	        expiry the record and its still-stored candidate fork are dropped
841	        together. Candidates submitted directly (no sync record) never expire,
842	        and an adopted tip is no longer in ``forks`` (it is on the canonical
843	        chain), so its expiring audit record leaves the chain untouched. A
844	        fork is dropped only when neither table still references it. If the
845	        write fails the pre-cleanup records and forks are restored so no
846	        success is ever reported for an un-persisted sweep. Caller must hold
847	        the store lock. Returns the pruned tip hashes.
848	        """
849	        plain_tips, plain_removed = self.store.prune_syncs()
850	        attested_tips, attested_removed = self.store.prune_attested_syncs()
851	        if not plain_removed and not attested_removed:
852	            return plain_tips + attested_tips
853	        expired_tips = plain_tips + attested_tips
854	        removed_forks: dict[str, list] = {}
855	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain}
856	        # The same tip could be referenced by another live record in either
857	        # table; only drop a fork nothing still points at.
858	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.syncs.values()}
859	        live_tips.update(
860	            rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.attested_syncs.values()
861	        )
862	        for tip in expired_tips:
863	            if tip in canonical_hashes or tip in live_tips:
864	                continue
865	            fork = self.store.forks.pop(tip, None)
866	            if fork is not None:
867	                removed_forks[tip] = fork
868	
869	        def append_expiry_events(
870	            removed: dict[tuple[str, str], dict], mode: str | None
871	        ) -> None:
872	            # Record one permanent expiry event per removed sync record. A tip
873	            # already adopted onto the canonical chain still gets its event:
874	            # the record's expiry is auditable even though the chain is
875	            # untouched. The event freezes the originally delivered summary.
876	            # Attested records' events carry mode="attested"; plain records
877	            # keep the historical shape with no mode.
878	            for (rec_source, request_id), rec in sorted(removed.items()):
879	                payload = {
880	                    "source": rec_source,
881	                    "request_id": request_id,
882	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
883	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
884	                    "height": rec.get("height"),
885	                    "length": rec.get("length"),
886	                    "status": rec.get("status"),
887	                }
888	                if mode is not None:
889	                    payload["mode"] = mode
890	                self.store.append_audit_event(EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED, payload)
891	
892	        append_expiry_events(plain_removed, None)
893	        append_expiry_events(attested_removed, SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED)
894	        removed_count = len(plain_removed) + len(attested_removed)
895	        try:
896	            self.store.save()
897	        except BaseException:
898	            # Restore the pre-cleanup state: a failed write must neither leave
899	            # the records gone nor their candidates orphaned, nor the events
900	            # durably visible.
901	            self.store.truncate_audit_events(removed_count)
902	            self.store.restore_syncs(plain_removed, removed_forks)
903	            self.store.restore_syncs(
904	                attested_removed, {}, table=self.store.attested_syncs
905	            )
906	            raise
907	        return expired_tips

909	    def _tip_descriptor(self, tip_hash: str) -> dict | None:

912	        Looks the candidate up among stored forks first, then among canonical
913	        blocks, so audit rows remain available after the candidate is adopted.
914	        """
915	        fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
916	        if fork is not None:
917	            return self._fork_summary(fork)
918	        for block in self.store.chain:
919	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
920	                return {
921	                    "tip_hash": block.block_hash,
922	                    "height": block.height,
923	                    # Length counts every block including the genesis block.
924	                    "length": block.height + 1,
925	                    "status": block.status,
926	                }

929	    def submit_fork_sync(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
930	        """POST /v1/forks/sync — receive a candidate chain from another node.
931

933	        seconds) and ``candidate`` (an export-format fork document).
934	
935	        Authorization. A *new* source+request_id pair is accepted only when the
936	        source is registered in the persistent trust registry with status
937	        ``active`` and an ``expires_at`` still in the future. An unknown,
938	        revoked or registry-expired source is rejected 403 before the candidate
939	        is examined. A retry on a still-live recorded key bypasses the registry
940	        check entirely: the recorded result must keep replaying even after the
941	        source has since been rotated, revoked or expired.
942	
943	        After authorization (and only then) the candidate is re-validated
944	        exactly like a direct candidate submission (canonical genesis,
945	        consecutive heights and prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and
946	        Merkle roots, tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique ascending tx_ids,
947	        endowment replay, pending-only-at-tip).
948

950	        source is 403; a well-formed new request whose ``expires_at`` is not
951	        later than now is 410; a well-formed but failing candidate chain (or a
952	        tampered candidate summary) is 400. Returns 201 on first acceptance
953	        with ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}``. A retry with
954	        the same source + request_id and identical content replays the original
955	        result as 200; the same key with different content returns 409, as does
956	        a duplicate tip already known.
957	        """
958	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
959	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
960	        for field in ("source", "request_id", "expires_at", "candidate"):
961	            if field not in payload:
962	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
963	
964	        source = payload["source"]
965	        request_id = payload["request_id"]
966	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
967	        candidate = payload["candidate"]
968	
969	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
970	            return 400, {"error": "field 'source' must be a non-empty string"}
971	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
972	            return 400, {"error": "field 'request_id' must be a non-empty string"}
973	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
974	            return 400, {"error": "field 'expires_at' must be a Unix-seconds integer"}

976	        blocks_raw = self._candidate_blocks(candidate)
977	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
978	            return 400, {"error": "field 'candidate' must contain a 'blocks' list"}
979	
980	        with self.store.lock:
981	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
982	
983	            key = (source, request_id)
984	            existing = self.store.syncs.get(key)
985	
986	            if existing is None:
987	                # Authorization gate for new deliveries only: the source must
988	                # be an active, unexpired entry of the persistent trust
989	                # registry. Unknown, revoked or registry-expired sources are
990	                # refused 403 before the candidate is examined. A retry on a
991	                # still-live key skips this, so a recorded result keeps
992	                # replaying even after the source has since been rotated,
993	                # revoked or expired.
994	                now = time.time()
995	                trusted = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
996	                if (
997	                    trusted is None
998	                    or trusted["status"] != TRUST_ACTIVE

1028	            canonical_blocks = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
1029	            fingerprint = self._candidate_fingerprint(canonical_blocks)
1030	
1031	            if existing is not None:

1034	                if fingerprint != existing["fingerprint"]:
1035	                    return 409, {
1036	                        "error": "request_id already used with different content"
1037	                    }
1038	                # Replay the ORIGINAL result frozen at first reception; only

1040	                descriptor: dict | None = None
1041	                if existing.get("height") is not None:

1043	                        "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
1044	                        "height": existing["height"],
1045	                        "length": existing["length"],
1046	                        "status": existing["status"],
1047	                    }

1051	                        "height": None,
1052	                        "length": None,

1061	                }
1062

1070	
1071	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork

1075	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,

1079	                "height": summary["height"],

1091	                    "length": summary["length"],

1111	    def submit_fork_sync_attested(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1112	        """POST /v1/forks/sync/attested — receive a signed candidate chain.
1113	
1114	        The request carries ``source``, ``request_id``, ``expires_at`` (Unix
1115	        seconds), ``candidate`` (an export object, a ``{"blocks": [...]}``
1116	        wrapper or a bare block array, kept in its delivered original form)
1117	        and ``signature`` — exactly 128 lowercase hex characters. The signed
1118	        message is the README canonical JSON of
1119	        ``{domain:"ledger-sync-v1", source, request_id, expires_at,
1120	        candidate}``; the signature is an Ed25519 signature over the raw
1121	        32-byte SHA-256 digest of those bytes, made with the source's current
1122	        registered public key.
1123	
1124	        Status precedence for a NEW key: malformed envelope fields (including
1125	        a signature that is not 128 lowercase hex characters) are 400; an
1126	        unauthorized source (unknown, revoked or registry-expired) is 403; a
1127	        well-formed request whose ``expires_at`` is not later than now is 410;
1128	        a signature that does not verify under the source's CURRENT registered
1129	        key/version is 403; then the candidate chain (and any supplied export
1130	        summary) is fully re-validated exactly like a plain sync, failure 400;
1131	        a tip already known as canonical or a stored candidate is 409.
1132

1927	    def _validate_trust_input(self, payload: object, require_version: bool) -> tuple | None:
1928	        """Validate a trust registration/rotation body.
1929	
1930	        ``source`` must be a non-empty string, ``public_key`` 64 lowercase
1931	        hex characters and ``expires_at`` a plain (non-boolean) integer.
1932	        Rotation/revocation additionally require a positive integer
1933	        ``expected_version``. Returns (source, public_key, expires_at[,
1934	        expected_version]) or None after sending a 400.
1935	        """
1936	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1937	            return None
1938	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
1939	            if field not in payload:
1940	                return None
1941	        source = payload["source"]
1942	        public_key = payload["public_key"]
1943	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
1944	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1945	            return None
1946	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1947	            return None
1948	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
1949	            return None
1950	        if not require_version:
1951	            return source, public_key, expires_at
1952	        expected_version = payload.get("expected_version")
1953	        if (
1954	            isinstance(expected_version, bool)
1955	            or not isinstance(expected_version, int)
1956	            or expected_version < 1
1957	        ):
1958	            return None
1959	        return source, public_key, expires_at, expected_version

1961	    def register_trust_source(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1962	        """POST /v1/trust/sources — register a trusted source.
1963	
1964	        A new source is created at version 1 with status ``active`` and the
1965	        change is persisted together with its audit event in one atomic write
1966	        (201). Re-posting the exact same (public_key, expires_at) content is
1967	        idempotent (200, the stored record unchanged); the same source with
1968	        different content conflicts (409).
1969	        """
1970	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1971	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1972	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
1973	            if field not in payload:
1974	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
1975	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(payload, require_version=False)
1976	        if parsed is None:
1977	            return 400, {
1978	                "error": "source must be a non-empty string, public_key 64 "
1979	                "lowercase hex characters and expires_at an integer"
1980	            }
1981	        source, public_key, expires_at = parsed
1982	        with self.store.lock:
1983	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
1984	            if existing is not None:
1985	                if (
1986	                    existing["public_key"] == public_key
1987	                    and existing["expires_at"] == expires_at
1988	                ):
1989	                    # Idempotent re-registration: the stored record is reported
1990	                    # unchanged, with no new version and no new audit event.
1991	                    return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)
1992	                return 409, {"error": "trust source already exists with different content"}
1993	            record = {
1994	                "public_key": public_key,
1995	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1996	                "version": 1,
1997	                "status": TRUST_ACTIVE,
1998	            }
1999	            self.store.trust_sources[source] = record
2000	            self.store.append_audit_event(
2001	                EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED,
2002	                {
2003	                    "source": source,
2004	                    "public_key": public_key,
2005	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
2006	                    "version": 1,
2007	                },
2008	            )
2009	            try:
2010	                self.store.save()
2011	            except BaseException:
2012	                # Undo both the registry change and its event together.
2013	                self.store.trust_sources.pop(source, None)
2014	                self.store.truncate_audit_events(1)
2015	                raise
2016	            return 201, self._trust_record(source, record)

2018	    def rotate_trust_source(self, source: object, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
2019	        """POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/rotate — install a new public key.
2020	
2021	        Requires ``public_key``, ``expires_at`` and ``expected_version``. An
2022	        unknown or already-revoked source returns 404; a stale
2023	        ``expected_version`` returns 409. A successful rotation increments the
2024	        version, keeps the source active and persists the change with an audit
2025	        event atomically.
2026	        """
2027	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
2028	            return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
2029	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
2030	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
2031	        for field in ("public_key", "expires_at", "expected_version"):
2032	            if field not in payload:
2033	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
2034	        body = dict(payload)
2035	        body["source"] = source
2036	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(body, require_version=True)
2037	        if parsed is None:
2038	            return 400, {
2039	                "error": "public_key must be 64 lowercase hex characters and "
2040	                "expires_at/expected_version integers"
2041	            }
2042	        _, public_key, expires_at, expected_version = parsed
2043	        with self.store.lock:
2044	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
2045	            if existing is None or existing["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED:
2046	                return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
2047	            if existing["version"] != expected_version:
2048	                return 409, {"error": "expected_version does not match the current version"}
2049	            old_record = dict(existing)
2050	            existing["public_key"] = public_key
2051	            existing["expires_at"] = expires_at
2052	            existing["version"] = old_record["version"] + 1
2053	            self.store.append_audit_event(
2054	                EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED,
2055	                {
2056	                    "source": source,
2057	                    "public_key": public_key,
2058	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
2059	                    "version": existing["version"],
2060	                },
2061	            )
2062	            try:
2063	                self.store.save()
2064	            except BaseException:
2065	                self.store.trust_sources[source] = old_record
2066	                self.store.truncate_audit_events(1)
2067	                raise
2068	            return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)

2123	        ``sources`` contains only active, unexpired entries in the light

2125	        ``allowlist`` is preserved verbatim; ``audit_signers`` lists every

2129	        that signed each checkpoint.

2139	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
2140	                }
2141	            audit_signers = [dict(entry) for entry in self.store.audit_signer_history]

2143	                "genesis_hash": self.store.chain[0].block_hash,

312	def cmd_sync_range(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
313	    try:
314	        if args.range_json == "-":
315	            document = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
316	        else:
317	            document = json.loads(args.range_json)
318	    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
319	        return _emit(400, {"error": f"invalid JSON range document: {exc}"})
320	    # The range document is {"anchor", "blocks"[, "tip"]}; a GET
321	    # /v1/chain/range page may be piped verbatim (its extra canonical/
322	    # next_height fields are ignored).
323	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
324	        return _emit(400, {"error": "range document must be a JSON object"})
325	    anchor = document.get("anchor")
326	    blocks = document.get("blocks")
327	    if not isinstance(anchor, dict) or not isinstance(blocks, list):
328	        return _emit(
329	            400, {"error": "range document must contain an anchor object and a blocks list"}
330	        )
331	    payload = {
332	        "source": args.source,
333	        "request_id": args.request_id,
334	        "expires_at": args.expires_at,
335	        "anchor": anchor,
336	        "blocks": blocks,
337	    }
338	    tip = document.get("tip")
339	    if tip is None and blocks:
340	        # Derive the tip summary from the final delivered block so a plain
341	        # range page (which carries no tip) can be pushed verbatim.
342	        last = blocks[-1]
343	        if isinstance(last, dict):
344	            anchor_height = anchor.get("height")
345	            length = (
346	                anchor_height + 1 + len(blocks)
347	                if isinstance(anchor_height, int) and not isinstance(anchor_height, bool)
348	                else None
349	            )
350	            tip = {
351	                "tip_hash": last.get("block_hash"),
352	                "height": last.get("height"),
353	                "length": length,
354	                "status": last.get("status"),
355	            }
356	    if tip is not None:
357	        payload["tip"] = tip
358	    status, body = _request("POST", f"{args.base_url}/v1/forks/sync/range", payload)
359	    return _emit(status, body)

362	def cmd_sync_attested(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
363	    try:
364	        if args.candidate_json == "-":
365	            candidate = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
366	        else:
367	            candidate = json.loads(args.candidate_json)
368	    except (ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
369	        return _emit(400, {"error": f"invalid JSON candidate: {exc}"})
370	    # Preserve the candidate's original form (export object, {"blocks": [...]}
371	    # wrapper or a bare block array): the signature is over the canonical
372	    # message embedding exactly that parsed value.
373	    if not isinstance(candidate, (dict, list)):
374	        return _emit(400, {"error": "candidate must be a JSON object or array"})
375	    document = {
376	        "domain": "ledger-sync-v1",
377	        "source": args.source,
378	        "request_id": args.request_id,
379	        "expires_at": args.expires_at,
380	        "candidate": candidate,
381	    }
382	    message = json.dumps(
383	        document, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")
384	    ).encode("utf-8")
385	    # Sign the raw 32-byte SHA-256 digest with the 64-lowercase-hex Ed25519
386	    # seed; the result is a 128-lowercase-hex signature.
387	    signature = crypto.sign_message(
388	        args.signing_key, hashlib.sha256(message).digest()
389	    )
390	    if signature is None:
391	        return _emit(400, {"error": "signing key must be 64 lowercase hex characters"})
392	    payload = {
393	        "source": args.source,
394	        "request_id": args.request_id,
395	        "expires_at": args.expires_at,
396	        "candidate": candidate,
397	        "signature": signature,
398	    }
399	    status, body = _request(
400	        "POST", f"{args.base_url}/v1/forks/sync/attested", payload
401	    )
402	    return _emit(status, body)

506	def cmd_audit_verify(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
507	    """Offline audit export verification; no server contact is made.
508	
509	    The input is one export page or a JSON array of pages (the pages of a
510	    full export, in order), read from ``FILE`` or standard input when the
511	    argument is ``-``. Prints a single JSON line:
512	    ``{"ok": true, "checkpoint": {...}}`` on success or
513	    ``{"ok": false, "error": "input"|"integrity"|"auth"}`` on failure, and
514	    exits 0/1 respectively.
515	
516	    Without ``--trust`` only the hash chain is checked. With a trust document
517	    its genesis anchor and ``audit_signers`` additionally authenticate every
518	    page's ``checkpoint_auth`` signature and bind the pages to one another.
519	    """
520	    from .audit import verify_export
521	
522	    try:
523	        if args.export_file == "-":
524	            document = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
525	        else:
526	            with open(args.export_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
527	                document = json.load(fh)
528	    except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
529	        # Unreadable or non-JSON input is an input error.
530	        body = {"ok": False, "error": "input"}
531	    else:
532	        trust = None
533	        if args.trust is not None:
534	            try:
535	                with open(args.trust, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
536	                    trust = json.load(fh)
537	            except (OSError, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
538	                body = {"ok": False, "error": "input"}
539	                print(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False))
540	                return 1
541	        body = verify_export(document, trust)
542	    print(json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False))
543	    return 0 if body.get("ok") is True else 1

1	"""Tests for GET /v1/forks/sync/history — the sync lifecycle history query.
2	
3	The history is backed by the append-only audit log and returns one row per
4	durable sync_received / sync_adopted / sync_expired event, each carrying the
5	tip summary frozen when the event was recorded. These tests cover parameter
6	validation (tip_hash/kind 400 vs. unknown-empty-page, strict non-negative
7	decimal parsing with no leading zeros/signs/whitespace/decimals, repeated
8	query parameters, limit 1-200 defaulting to 50, min_height > max_height and
9	cursor > total -> 400, cursor == total -> empty page), the
10	(height, tip_hash, source, request_id, event_id) ordering, pagination via
11	next_cursor, frozen-summary immutability across adoption and expiry (an
12	adopted-then-expired record leaves the canonical chain untouched), restart
13	persistence and legacy-snapshot compatibility (records/events written before
14	frozen summaries still load and resolve), plus the HTTP and CLI surfaces.
15	
16	Run: python3 tests/sync_history_test.py
17	"""

"""Tests for GET /v1/forks/sync/history — the sync lifecycle history query.

The history is backed by the append-only audit log and returns one row per
durable sync_received / sync_adopted / sync_expired event, each carrying the
tip summary frozen when the event was recorded. These tests cover parameter
validation (tip_hash/kind 400 vs. unknown-empty-page, strict non-negative
decimal parsing with no leading zeros/signs/whitespace/decimals, repeated
query parameters, limit 1-200 defaulting to 50, min_height > max_height and
cursor > total -> 400, cursor == total -> empty page), the
(height, tip_hash, source, request_id, event_id) ordering, pagination via
next_cursor, frozen-summary immutability across adoption and expiry (an
adopted-then-expired record leaves the canonical chain untouched), restart
persistence and legacy-snapshot compatibility (records/events written before
frozen summaries still load and resolve), plus the HTTP and CLI surfaces.

Run: python3 tests/sync_history_test.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

from ledger import crypto
from ledger.cli import main as cli_main
from ledger.models import Block, Transaction
from ledger.server import build_handler
from ledger.service import LedgerService
from ledger.store import LedgerStore, StateRecoveryError


def keypair() -> tuple[Ed25519PrivateKey, str]:
    key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub = key.public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
    ).hex()
    return key, pub


def tx_obj(key: Ed25519PrivateKey, sender: str, to: str, amount: int) -> Transaction:
    msg = crypto.canonical_message(sender, to, amount)
    return Transaction.from_dict(
        {"from": sender, "to": to, "amount": amount, "signature": key.sign(msg).hex()}
    )


def make_fork(genesis: Block, blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
    tip = blocks[-1]
    return {
        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
        "height": tip.height,
        "length": len(blocks),
        "status": tip.status,
        "blocks": [b.to_dict() for b in blocks],
    }


class HistoryServiceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.state_path = os.path.join(self.tmp, "state.json")
        self.svc = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        self.store = self.svc.store
        self.genesis = self.store.chain[0]
        self.ka, self.A = keypair()
        self.kb, self.B = keypair()
        self.kc, self.C = keypair()
        self._trust_seq = 0

    def _trust(self, source: str) -> None:
        self._trust_seq += 1
        key_hex = format(0x1000 + self._trust_seq, "064x")
        status, _ = self.svc.register_trust_source(
            {
                "source": source,
                "public_key": key_hex,
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 10_000_000,
            }
        )
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 201))

    def _block1(self, amount: int, to: str | None = None, *, status: str = "confirmed") -> Block:
        return Block.create(
            1,
            self.genesis.block_hash,
            [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, to or self.B, amount)],
            status,
        )

    def _sync_block1(
        self, source: str, request_id: str, amount: int, to: str | None = None
    ) -> dict:
        self._trust(source)
        block = self._block1(amount, to)
        status, body = self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": source,
                "request_id": request_id,
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 3600,
                "candidate": make_fork(self.genesis, [self.genesis, block]),
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        return body

    def _history(self, **params) -> tuple[int, dict]:
        return self.svc.list_fork_sync_history(params)

    # -- basics / validation ------------------------------------------------

    def test_empty_history_is_empty_page(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._history()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"items": [], "total": 0, "next_cursor": None})

    def test_unknown_tip_hash_is_empty_page_malformed_is_400(self) -> None:
        status, body = self._history(tip_hash="f" * 64)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["total"], 0)
        for bad in ("", "z" * 64, "A" * 64, "0" * 63, "0" * 65, "  " + "0" * 64, 123):
            self.assertEqual(self._history(tip_hash=bad)[0], 400, bad)

    def test_kind_filter_and_unknown_kind_400(self) -> None:
        self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        for kind in ("sync_received", "sync_adopted", "sync_expired"):
            status, body = self._history(kind=kind)
            self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(self._history(kind="sync_adopted")[1]["total"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(self._history(kind="sync_received")[1]["total"], 1)
        for bad in ("received", "SYNC_RECEIVED", "", "sync_received "):
            self.assertEqual(self._history(kind=bad)[0], 400, bad)

    def test_numeric_params_strict_decimal(self) -> None:
        bad_values = ("01", "-1", "+1", "1 ", " 1", "1.0", "x", "")
        for name in ("min_height", "max_height", "cursor"):
            for bad in bad_values:
                self.assertEqual(self._history(**{name: bad})[0], 400, (name, bad))
        for bad in ("0", "201", "01", "-1", "1.0"):
            self.assertEqual(self._history(limit=bad)[0], 400, bad)
        for good in ("1", "50", "200", "0"):
            # limit=0 is rejected; everything else parses (an over-total
            # cursor is validated separately below).
            status = self._history(
                **{"limit" if good in ("1", "50", "200") else "cursor": good}
            )[0]
            self.assertEqual(status, 200, good)

    def test_height_range_and_cursor_rules(self) -> None:
        self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        self.assertEqual(self._history(min_height="1", max_height="1")[1]["total"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(self._history(min_height="2")[1]["total"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(self._history(min_height="2", max_height="1")[0], 400)
        # cursor == total -> empty page; cursor > total -> 400.
        self.assertEqual(
            self._history(cursor="1")[1],
            {"items": [], "total": 1, "next_cursor": None},
        )
        self.assertEqual(self._history(cursor="2")[0], 400)

    # -- item shape / ordering / pagination ---------------------------------

    def test_received_row_shape_and_frozen_summary(self) -> None:
        body = self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        _, page = self._history()
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        item = page["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual(
            set(item),
            {
                "event_id",
                "kind",
                "at",
                "source",
                "request_id",
                "tip_hash",
                "height",
                "length",
                "status",
                "expires_at",
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(item["kind"], "sync_received")
        self.assertEqual(item["event_id"], 2)  # event 1 is source_registered
        self.assertEqual(item["source"], "node-1")
        self.assertEqual(item["request_id"], "r1")
        self.assertEqual(item["tip_hash"], body["tip_hash"])
        self.assertEqual(item["height"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(item["length"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(item["status"], "confirmed")
        self.assertEqual(item["expires_at"], body["expires_at"])
        self.assertIsInstance(item["at"], (int, float))

    def test_ordering_and_pagination(self) -> None:
        # Three height-1 tips from distinct sources plus one height-2 tip.
        b1 = self._sync_block1("s1", "r1", 10)
        b2 = self._sync_block1("s2", "r2", 20, self.C)
        b3 = self._sync_block1("s3", "r3", 30)
        # A two-block candidate: A->B 5 at height 1, then B->C 2 at height 2.
        self._trust("s4")
        h1 = Block.create(
            1,
            self.genesis.block_hash,
            [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 5)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        h2 = Block.create(
            2, h1.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.kb, self.B, self.C, 2)], "confirmed"
        )
        status, b4 = self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": "s4",
                "request_id": "r4",
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 3600,
                "candidate": make_fork(self.genesis, [self.genesis, h1, h2]),
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, b4)

        _, page = self._history(limit="200")
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 4)
        ordered = [
            (it["height"], it["tip_hash"], it["source"], it["request_id"], it["event_id"])
            for it in page["items"]
        ]
        self.assertEqual(ordered, sorted(ordered))
        # The height-2 row sorts last regardless of source/event order.
        self.assertEqual(page["items"][-1]["tip_hash"], b4["tip_hash"])
        # The three height-1 rows are tip_hash ordered.
        height1_tips = sorted([b1["tip_hash"], b2["tip_hash"], b3["tip_hash"]])
        self.assertEqual(
            [it["tip_hash"] for it in page["items"][:3]], height1_tips
        )
        # Pagination: pages of 2, next_cursor walks 0 -> 2 -> None.
        _, first = self._history(limit="2", cursor="0")
        self.assertEqual(len(first["items"]), 2)
        self.assertEqual(first["total"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(first["next_cursor"], 2)
        _, second = self._history(limit="2", cursor="2")
        self.assertEqual([it["tip_hash"] for it in second["items"]],
                         [it["tip_hash"] for it in page["items"][2:]])
        self.assertIsNone(second["next_cursor"])

    def test_source_filter(self) -> None:
        self._sync_block1("s1", "r1", 10)
        self._sync_block1("s2", "r2", 20)
        _, page = self._history(source="s1")
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(page["items"][0]["source"], "s1")
        self.assertEqual(self._history(source="")[0], 400)

    # -- lifecycle: adoption and expiry freeze past rows --------------------

    def test_adoption_adds_row_without_rewriting_received(self) -> None:
        # Canonical confirmed block 1 so a length-3 synced fork can win.
        canon = Block.create(
            1,
            self.genesis.block_hash,
            [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.C, 1)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        self.store.chain.append(canon)
        self.store.rebuild_derived()
        self.store.save()
        f1 = Block.create(
            1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 10)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        f2 = Block.create(
            2, f1.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.kb, self.B, self.C, 4)], "confirmed"
        )
        self._trust("node-1")
        status, body = self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": "node-1",
                "request_id": "req-1",
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 3600,
                "candidate": make_fork(self.genesis, [self.genesis, f1, f2]),
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.adopt_fork(tip)[0], 200)

        _, page = self._history()
        kinds = [it["kind"] for it in page["items"]]
        self.assertIn("sync_received", kinds)
        self.assertIn("sync_adopted", kinds)
        received = next(it for it in page["items"] if it["kind"] == "sync_received")
        adopted = next(it for it in page["items"] if it["kind"] == "sync_adopted")
        # One adopted row per source provenance entry.
        self.assertEqual(kinds.count("sync_adopted"), 1)
        for row in (received, adopted):
            self.assertEqual(row["tip_hash"], tip)
            self.assertEqual(row["height"], 2)
            self.assertEqual(row["length"], 3)
            self.assertEqual(row["status"], "confirmed")
        self.assertNotEqual(received["event_id"], adopted["event_id"])

    def test_expiry_adds_row_and_keeps_frozen_history(self) -> None:
        exp = int(time.time()) + 3600
        body = self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]
        received_before = self._history(kind="sync_received")[1]["items"][0]

        # Force the record past its deadline in place of waiting for wall time.
        self.store.syncs[("node-1", "r1")]["expires_at"] = int(time.time()) - 5
        self.store.save()
        _, page = self._history()  # triggers the lazy sweep
        kinds = [it["kind"] for it in page["items"]]
        self.assertEqual(kinds, ["sync_received", "sync_expired"])
        expired = next(it for it in page["items"] if it["kind"] == "sync_expired")
        self.assertEqual(expired["tip_hash"], tip)
        self.assertEqual(expired["height"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(expired["length"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(expired["status"], "confirmed")
        # The received row is byte-for-byte the same history entry.
        received_after = self._history(kind="sync_received")[1]["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual(received_after, received_before)
        # Candidate and metadata are gone but history rows remain.
        self.assertNotIn(("node-1", "r1"), self.store.syncs)
        self.assertNotIn(tip, self.store.forks)
        # A second sweep produces no duplicate expiry event.
        self.assertEqual(
            self._history()[1]["items"].count(
                self._history(kind="sync_expired")[1]["items"][0]
            ),
            1,
        )

    def test_adopted_tip_expiry_leaves_canonical_and_history(self) -> None:
        # Canonical length 2; synced fork length 3 wins and is adopted.
        c1 = Block.create(
            1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.C, 1)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        c2 = Block.create(
            2, c1.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.C, 1)], "confirmed"
        )
        self.store.chain.extend([c1, c2])
        self.store.rebuild_derived()
        self.store.save()
        f1 = Block.create(
            1, self.genesis.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, self.B, 10)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        f2 = Block.create(
            2, f1.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.kb, self.B, self.C, 4)], "confirmed"
        )
        f3 = Block.create(
            3, f2.block_hash, [tx_obj(self.kc, self.C, self.B, 1)], "confirmed"
        )
        self._trust("node-1")
        status, body = self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": "node-1",
                "request_id": "req-1",
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 3600,
                "candidate": make_fork(self.genesis, [self.genesis, f1, f2, f3]),
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]
        self.assertEqual(self.svc.adopt_fork(tip)[0], 200)
        # Expire the now-adopted record; canonical must not change.
        self.store.syncs[("node-1", "req-1")]["expires_at"] = int(time.time()) - 5
        self.store.save()
        self._history()
        self.assertEqual(self.store.tip_hash(), tip)
        kinds = [it["kind"] for it in self._history()[1]["items"]]
        self.assertEqual(
            sorted(kinds), ["sync_adopted", "sync_expired", "sync_received"]
        )

    # -- restart persistence and legacy compatibility -----------------------

    def test_history_survives_restart(self) -> None:
        body = self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        rec = data["syncs"][0]
        for field in ("height", "length", "status"):
            self.assertIn(field, rec)
        self.assertEqual((rec["height"], rec["length"], rec["status"]), (1, 2, "confirmed"))

        reopened = LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000)
        svc2 = LedgerService(reopened, initial_balance=1000)
        _, page = svc2.list_fork_sync_history({})
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        item = page["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual(item["tip_hash"], tip)
        self.assertEqual((item["height"], item["length"], item["status"]),
                         (1, 2, "confirmed"))

    def test_legacy_snapshot_without_frozen_summaries_loads(self) -> None:
        self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        # Simulate a pre-feature snapshot: no frozen summary anywhere.
        for rec in data["syncs"]:
            for field in ("height", "length", "status"):
                rec.pop(field, None)
        for event in data["audit_events"]:
            if event.get("kind") == "sync_received":
                for field in ("height", "length", "status"):
                    event.pop(field, None)
        # Dropping payload fields invalidates any stored event_hash, so model
        # the older snapshot honestly: no audit hash links and no checkpoint
        # either; recovery backfills them once on the winning snapshot.
        for event in data["audit_events"]:
            event.pop("prev_hash", None)
            event.pop("event_hash", None)
        data.pop("audit_checkpoint", None)
        with open(self.state_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(data, fh)

        reopened = LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000)
        # The live record is repaired from its surviving candidate.
        rec = reopened.syncs[("node-1", "r1")]
        self.assertEqual((rec["height"], rec["length"], rec["status"]),
                         (1, 2, "confirmed"))
        # The legacy event resolves live and still reports the right summary.
        svc2 = LedgerService(reopened, initial_balance=1000)
        _, page = svc2.list_fork_sync_history({})
        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        item = page["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual((item["height"], item["length"], item["status"]),
                         (1, 2, "confirmed"))

    def test_corrupt_history_metadata_fails_recovery(self) -> None:
        self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        with open(self.state_path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            data = json.load(fh)
        data["audit_events"][-1]["tip_hash"] = "z" * 64
        out = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "state.json")
        with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(data, fh)
        with self.assertRaises(StateRecoveryError):
            LedgerStore(out, initial_balance=1000)

    def test_backfilled_expiry_event_carries_frozen_summary(self) -> None:
        body = self._sync_block1("node-1", "r1", 10)
        tip = body["tip_hash"]

        self.assertEqual(page["total"], 1)
        item = page["items"][0]
        self.assertEqual(item["tip_hash"], tip)
        self.assertEqual((item["height"], item["length"], item["status"]),
                         (1, 2, "confirmed"))

                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))

# signature-attested endpoint (/v1/forks/sync/attested) share one record table
# but keep separate idempotency namespaces via a 3-key (mode, source,

SYNC_MODE_PLAIN = "plain"

# Domain separator of the attested-sync signature message; it binds a
# signature to this protocol so the same key's signatures elsewhere never
# verify as an attestation.
ATTESTED_DOMAIN = "ledger-sync-v1"

# Audit event kinds are owned by the store layer (recovery emits them too);
# service.EVENT_* constants mirror these literal values.
EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED = "sync_received"
EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED = "sync_adopted"
EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED = "sync_expired"
EVENT_AUDIT_SIGNER_ROTATED = "audit_signer_rotated"
EVENT_ALLOWLIST_ADDED = "allowlist_added"
EVENT_ALLOWLIST_REMOVED = "allowlist_removed"

# Prefix of durable snapshot temp files ("<state>.ledger-<...>") living next to
# the main state file. They double as crash-recovery candidates on startup.
SNAPSHOT_PREFIX = ".ledger-"

# Fallback per-identity endowment used only for snapshots written before
# state.initial_balance was recorded; mirrors service.DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
# without importing the service layer (which imports this module).
DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE = 1_000_000


def attested_message(
    source: str,
    request_id: str,
    expires_at: int,
    candidate: object,
) -> bytes:
    """Canonical bytes signed by an attested-sync delivery.

    The document is exactly
    ``{domain:"ledger-sync-v1", source, request_id, expires_at, candidate}``
    serialized README-style (``sort_keys``, compact separators,
    ``ensure_ascii=False``). ``candidate`` is embedded in its original form
    (an export object, a ``{"blocks": [...]}`` wrapper or a bare block array),
    so the signature binds the exact JSON value the sender signed rather than a
    re-parsed/re-serialized approximation of it.
    """
    document = {
        "domain": ATTESTED_DOMAIN,
        "source": source,
        "request_id": request_id,
        "expires_at": expires_at,
        "candidate": candidate,
    }
    return json.dumps(
        document, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":")
    ).encode("utf-8")


def attested_fingerprint(
    source: str,
    request_id: str,
    expires_at: int,
    candidate: object,
    signature: str,
) -> str:
    """Content fingerprint of an attested delivery's signed original form.

    Covers the exact signed message (candidate in its delivered raw form) plus
    the signature itself. It lets same-key retries and restart reconciliation
    detect any tampering with the envelope, the candidate or the signature.
    """
    message = attested_message(source, request_id, expires_at, candidate)
    return hashlib.sha256(message + signature.encode("ascii")).hexdigest()

  十进制（`0` 合法），非法值 `400`，`min_height > max_height` 也是 `400`。合并
  结果按 `(height, tip_hash, source, mode, request_id)` 升序稳定分页，返回
  `{items, total, next_cursor}`；
  `cursor == total` 返回空页，`cursor > total` 返回 `400`，没有更多结果时
  `next_cursor` 为 `null`。每个 item 保留原七字段
  `{source, request_id, tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}`，不含
  `mode`。

  每个同步生命周期的每个阶段一行。支持 `source`、`tip_hash`、`kind`、`mode`、
  `min_height`、`max_height`、`limit`（默认 50，范围 1–200）、`cursor`（默认
  0）。`tip_hash` 必须是 64 位小写十六进制：格式错误 `400`，未知值只返回空页；
  `kind` 只允许 `sync_received`、`sync_adopted`、`sync_expired`，未知值 `400`。
  `mode` 缺省或 `all` 返回全量事件；`plain` 匹配普通事件（含没有 `mode` 字段
  的旧事件——旧事件仍按既有字段输出、不新增字段）；`attested` 仅匹配
  `mode="attested"` 的事件；非法或重复 `mode` 返回 `400`。
  数值参数必须是非负十进制字符串——除 `0` 外禁止前导零，符号、小数、空白及重复
  参数一律 `400`；`min_height > max_height` 或 `cursor > total` 也是 `400`，

"""Tests for inter-node candidate-chain sync and the audit query.

Covers POST /v1/forks/sync (envelope validation, full candidate re-validation
reusing the fork rules, 201 success with the five result fields, 410 on an
expired request, 400 on malformed/input or a failing chain check, 200
same-source+request_id identical-content retry returning the original result,
409 on same-key different content and on a duplicate tip), GET /v1/forks/sync
(source/min_height/max_height/limit/cursor filters, strict decimal parsing,
(height, tip_hash, source) ordering, items/total/next_cursor pagination with
cursor == total -> empty page and cursor > total -> 400), expiry-driven
removal of the delivered candidate, serialization against adoption, adoption
of a winning synced fork (longest chain / smallest tip hash, atomic swap,
old-chain confirmed txs returning to the mempool while pending txs stay out),
restart re-validation/expiry handling (records expiring while down are pruned
and each gets one deduplicated, densely-id'd sync_expired backfilled and
persisted atomically; a second restart does not repeat it), and the HTTP +
CLI surfaces.

Run: python3 tests/fork_sync_test.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import io
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from http.server import ThreadingHTTPServer

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

from ledger import crypto
from ledger.cli import main as cli_main
from ledger.models import Block, Transaction
from ledger.server import build_handler
from ledger.service import LedgerService
from ledger.store import LedgerStore


def keypair() -> tuple[Ed25519PrivateKey, str]:
    key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub = key.public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
    ).hex()
    return key, pub


def signed_tx(key: Ed25519PrivateKey, sender: str, to: str, amount: int) -> dict:
    msg = crypto.canonical_message(sender, to, amount)
    return {"from": sender, "to": to, "amount": amount, "signature": key.sign(msg).hex()}


def tx_obj(key: Ed25519PrivateKey, sender: str, to: str, amount: int) -> Transaction:
    return Transaction.from_dict(signed_tx(key, sender, to, amount))


def make_fork(genesis: Block, blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
    """Build an export-format candidate document for the given block list."""
    tip = blocks[-1]
    return {
        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
        "height": tip.height,
        "length": len(blocks),
        "status": tip.status,
        "blocks": [b.to_dict() for b in blocks],
    }


class ForkSyncServiceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.state_path = os.path.join(self.tmp, "state.json")
        self.svc = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        self.store = self.svc.store
        self.genesis = self.store.chain[0]
        self.ka, self.A = keypair()
        self.kb, self.B = keypair()
        self.kc, self.C = keypair()
        # Sources used through the sync() helper are registered as active,
        # far-future trusted sources. Tests for the authorization gate register
        # (or deliberately leave unregistered) sources by hand.
        self._trusted: set[str] = set()
        self._trust_seq = 0

"""Tests for the optional ``mode`` query parameter on
GET /v1/forks/sync and GET /v1/forks/sync/history.

For GET /v1/forks/sync: absent or ``plain`` lists only ordinary syncs,
``attested`` only signature-attested syncs and ``all`` merges both tables,
ordered by (height, tip_hash, source, mode, request_id); items keep the
historical seven fields; invalid values and repeated parameters are 400.

For GET /v1/forks/sync/history: absent or ``all`` returns every event,
``plain`` matches ordinary events including legacy rows with no mode field,
``attested`` matches only mode="attested" events; invalid/repeated mode is
400; event output fields are unchanged.

Run: python3 tests/sync_mode_query_test.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import io
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile

import time
import unittest

import urllib.request

from ledger import crypto

from ledger.server import build_handler
from ledger.service import LedgerService
from ledger.store import LedgerStore, attested_message


def keypair() -> tuple[Ed25519PrivateKey, str]:
    key = Ed25519PrivateKey.generate()
    pub = key.public_key().public_bytes(
        serialization.Encoding.Raw, serialization.PublicFormat.Raw
    ).hex()
    return key, pub


def tx_obj(key: Ed25519PrivateKey, sender: str, to: str, amount: int) -> Transaction:
    msg = crypto.canonical_message(sender, to, amount)
    return Transaction.from_dict(
        {"from": sender, "to": to, "amount": amount, "signature": key.sign(msg).hex()}
    )


def make_fork(blocks: list[Block]) -> dict:
    tip = blocks[-1]
    return {
        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
        "height": tip.height,

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        self.state_path = os.path.join(self.tmp, "state.json")
        self.svc = LedgerService(
            LedgerStore(self.state_path, initial_balance=1000), initial_balance=1000
        )
        self.store = self.svc.store
        self.genesis = self.store.chain[0]
        self.ka, self.A = keypair()
        self.kb, self.B = keypair()
        self.kc, self.C = keypair()

    def _register(self, source: str, pub: str) -> None:
        status, body = self.svc.register_trust_source(

                "source": source,
                "public_key": pub,
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 10_000_000,
            }
        )
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 201), body)

    def _plain_sync(
        self, source: str, request_id: str, block: Block
    ) -> tuple[int, dict]:
        return self.svc.submit_fork_sync(
            {
                "source": source,
                "request_id": request_id,
                "expires_at": int(time.time()) + 3600,
                "candidate": make_fork([self.genesis, block]),
            }

    def _attested_sync(
        self,
        source: str,
        request_id: str,
        block: Block,
        key: Ed25519PrivateKey,

        expires_at = int(time.time()) + 3600
        message = attested_message(source, request_id, expires_at, candidate)
        signature = crypto.sign_message(
            key, hashlib.sha256(message).digest()  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        )

        return self.svc.submit_fork_sync_attested(
            {

                "request_id": request_id,
                "expires_at": expires_at,
                "candidate": candidate,
                "signature": signature,

        )

            self.assertNotEqual(body["items"][0]["tip_hash"], att_tip)

        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["total"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(body["items"][0]["tip_hash"], att_tip)

            )

        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        for item in body["items"]:
            self.assertEqual(
                set(item),
                {
                    "source",
                    "request_id",
                    "tip_hash",
                    "height",
                    "length",
                    "status",
                    "expires_at",

        # Two records with the same (height, tip_hash) cannot exist, but
        # same-height distinct tips from both modes must interleave by

                [tx_obj(self.ka, self.A, to, 5 + idx)],
                "confirmed",
            )

        self.assertEqual(st, 201, pb0)
        st, pb1 = self._plain_sync("s2", "rp1", blocks["p1"])
        self.assertEqual(st, 201, pb1)
        ak, ap = keypair()
        att0 = Block.create(
            1,
            self.genesis.block_hash,
            [tx_obj(self.kb, self.B, self.C, 7)],
            "confirmed",
        )
        st, ab0 = self._attested_sync("s3", "ra0", att0, ak, ap)
        self.assertEqual(st, 201, ab0)

        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["total"], 3)
        keys = [

                item["tip_hash"],
